name: Combined Immunodeficiency Due to ITK Deficiency

ethnicAssociations: Reported in diverse ethnic groups including Middle Eastern and European populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for ITK Deficiency

criteria.description: Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in the ITK gene
Reduced or absent CD8+ T cell counts and impaired T cell activation
Recurrent severe viral infections, particularly Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) associated lymphoproliferation
Defective T cell receptor (TCR) signaling demonstrated by functional assays
Consanguinity or affected siblings with similar immunodeficiency

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of biallelic pathogenic ITK variants plus clinical features of combined immunodeficiency with impaired CD8+ T cell function
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of genetic, immunological, and clinical data; functional assays support diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Often presents as persistent infectious mononucleosis or lymphoma
Marked reduction in cytotoxic T lymphocytes
searchTerms: very low CD8 T cell counts
profound deficiency of CD8 immune cells
severe lack of cytotoxic T cells

pathognomonic.notes: Demonstrated by defective calcium flux and activation markers
searchTerms: problems with T cell receptor signaling

common.symptomName: Recurrent severe viral infections (e.g., herpesviruses, respiratory viruses)
common.notes: Includes CMV, HSV, and respiratory viral infections
searchTerms: repeated severe viral infections like herpes and respiratory viruses

common.notes: Enlargement of liver and spleen due to lymphoproliferation
Poor growth in infancy and early childhood

occasional.notes: Chronic inflammation and fibrosis of lung tissue
Fungal infection of the oral mucosa

rare.symptomName: Neurological complications secondary to CNS lymphoproliferation
searchTerms: brain problems from lymph node growth in CNS
neurological issues due to CNS lymphoproliferation
nerve complications from CNS immune cell expansion

rare.notes: Skin lesions caused by viral pathogens

laboratory: Elevated EBV viral load in blood
Impaired T cell proliferation and activation assays
imaging: Lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly on ultrasound or CT
Interstitial lung changes on chest CT

distinguishingFeatures: Severe EBV-driven disease with normal ITK function
Profound T and B cell deficiency
Multiple genetic causes other than ITK
Early infancy onset with severe opportunistic infections

redFlags: Severe EBV-associated lymphoproliferative disease in early childhood
Profound CD8+ T cell lymphopenia with recurrent viral infections
Family history of early childhood deaths from infections or lymphoproliferation
references: Stepensky P, et al. ITK deficiency causes combined immunodeficiency with EBV-driven lymphoproliferation. J Clin Invest. 2015.
Huck K, et al. Combined immunodeficiency due to ITK mutations: clinical and immunological features. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2017.
Orphanet: Combined immunodeficiency due to ITK deficiency (ORPHA:538963)
